title: Common platform primitives
description: Shared definitions referenced by the other contracts. Nothing here is a message in its own right.

runId.description: Opaque identifier of a graph run.

nodeId.description: Identifier of a node within a graph definition. Unique within the definition.

attempt.description: 1-based attempt counter within one iteration of a node. A retry increments it (ADR-0008 §11, ADR-0021 §2). The retry budget is scoped per iteration, so each iteration starts again at 1.

iteration.description: 1-based loop iteration counter (ADR-0021 §2). Nodes outside a loop are always on iteration 1; there is no zero and no absent case, so the NodeRun key is uniform. Together with attempt this distinguishes 'the second try at round one' from 'the first try at round two', which a single counter cannot.

relativePath.description: A canonical workspace-relative path (ADR-0023 §2). The first segment is always a repositoryId, because the workspace holds one directory per repository. Non-canonical paths are rejected, never normalised: normalising before an authorization decision is the standard traversal-bypass pattern, so exactly one spelling of a path is accepted. NFC normalisation is required but is not expressible as a pattern and is enforced by the tool layer.

workspaceId.description: Opaque workspace token. ADR-0003 §3: anything that parses this value is a defect. It is deliberately not given a structured pattern.

executionHandle.description: Opaque handle returned by submit(). Not parseable by callers.

toolId.description: Stable namespaced tool identifier, e.g. github.pull_request.create (ADR-0005 §2).

repositoryId.description: Platform-assigned repository identifier. ADR-0014 §1: never derived from the remote URL.

costUnits.description: ADR-0026 §1. One cost unit is one micro-unit of the run's currency: 1 000 000 cost units is 1.00 of the ISO 4217 currency named on the GraphRun. Integers rather than decimals because ADR-0020 bans non-integers from hashed documents, and because float accumulation across thousands of calls makes a spending limit approximate — which for a spending limit is the same as unenforced. Provider amounts finer than a micro-unit are rounded up at record time, so the platform never under-reports spend.

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context traceparent header value (ADR-0015).

sideEffectClass.description: ADR-0005 §3. Ordered from least to most consequential; a grant may narrow, never widen.

failureCategory.description: ADR-0008 §11, extended by ADR-0009. Retry is driven by category, never by message text.

correlation.description: Telemetry correlation block. ADR-0003 §4: carried, never interpreted. ADR-0015 §7: these values are forbidden as metric labels. Carries the full four-part NodeRun key (ADR-0021 §6) so a log line, a span and a stored record name the same thing.

pathScopeEntry.description: Allow/deny globs for one repository. Globs are repository-relative: 'src/**' inside this entry can only ever mean that path inside the repository the entry is keyed by. Glob semantics are restricted (ADR-0023 §4): '*' matches within one segment, '**' matches whole segments, and there is no brace expansion or regular-expression syntax.

pathScope.description: Path authority, keyed by repositoryId (ADR-0023 §3). Keying by repository is what makes DEF-02 structurally impossible: under a flat glob list, 'src/**' matched every repository in the workspace, so a grant for one repository silently authorised the same paths in another. Here, authority for a repository is not expressible unless that repository is a key. Evaluation is default-deny and deny wins (ADR-0023 §4).

networkPolicy.description: ADR-0003 §3: mandatory on every execution request, so connectivity is a decision rather than a default.

repoRef.description: Identifies what to materialise into a workspace. With baseSha and the patch series this reconstructs a workspace (ADR-0003 §6).

jsonSchema.description: An embedded JSON Schema document. Not constrained further here; validated by the schema library at load time.
